messages:
maya: Heads up — customer Lark reported embedding drift after we merged their LoRA and quantized to int4. Quick eval pack is in the thread, numbers look off.
ravi: how big is the drift? cosine/pair numbers?
maya: avg cosine drop ~0.12 on the NQ probe set (same prompts pre-merge vs post-merge+int4). top-1 retrieval down ~6%.
anya: oh. Did you run with the same tokenizer/merge ordering? sometimes token remap + quant changes values.
maya: using our standard merge flow: base + lora -> merge_weights -> int4 with qconfig=v2. Tokenizer is the customer's pinned vocab; I included the merge command in the pack.
maya: pack snippet:
```bash
python tools/merge_lora.py --base models/llama-13b --lora customer/lark-lora --out merged/llama-13b-lark
python quantize.py --model merged/llama-13b-lark --bits 4 --qconfig qconfigs/v2.json
python eval_embed.py --model merged/llama-13b-lark-int4 --pairs eval/nq_pairs.json --out reports/lark-int4.csv
```
ravi: can you dump raw embedding vectors for a few failing pairs? want to check sign flips / scale changes.
maya: uploaded vectors: s3://redwood-qa/lark/emb-dumps/1712348901/
anya: quick sanity: compare L2 norms pre/post. int4 sometimes rescales per-row — we should check per-token norm distribution.
ci-bot: CI check: embedding-regression test for lark failed on branch release/quant-fixes (job #4821). See logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/4821
ravi: also verify KV cache layout — if merge changed attention bias ordering we can get drift in contextualized reps.
maya: checked KV shapes; they match. But noticed tokenizer did a fallback mapping on 3 tokens -> ▁ sequences for a handful of rare tokens in customer vocab.
anya: that can change prefix patterns, which affects embeddings. Can you rerun merge forcing byte-level mapping and compare? e.g. --force-bpe-map
maya: re-run queued with --force-bpe-map, will post results in ~10m.
ops-bot: deploy note: don't push merged model to staging until triage complete — tagging as on-hold.
ravi: if force-bpe-map fixes it, we should add a preflight that rejects merges where tokenizer remap occurs, or auto-normalize mapping.
anya: agreed. Also add small unit that compares tokenization between base and merged model for the eval prompts.
maya: first re-run finished: cosine drop reduced to 0.03, top-1 down 1.2%. Looks much better.
maya: attaching quick diff: s3://redwood-qa/lark/emb-diffs/1712348901/fix-vs-original.csv
ravi: great. next steps: (1) add tokenizer-mapping preflight, (2) fail merge if remap > threshold and suggest --force-bpe-map, (3) add CI regression for customer-specific quickpacks.
anya: I'll file a short RFC for the preflight and a small PR for the merge tool. assign to me + ravi.
maya: thanks — I'll keep the thread updated if the customer sees any downstream issues.
ci-bot: Automated note: created issue MLENG-1287: "Tokenizer-remap preflight for LoRA merges" (assignee: anya).
ops-bot: Reminder: retention policy requires we move QA dumps to long-term bucket if customer signs off.
maya: noted. :thumbsup:
